results.content: Annual inflation in the euro zone rose to 3.8% in September, beating market expectations to hit its highest level since September 2023. Last month's print is up from the 3.2% recorded in August, above the 3.6% forecast by markets and well ahead of the European Central Bank's 2% target. Core inflation came in at 2.5%, in line with expectations. The move was fueled by soaring energy prices caused by the ongoing Middle East conflict. This is a developing story.
results.title: Eurozone inflation hits its highest level in three years at 3.8% - CNBC

results.content: US consumer sentiment fell to its second-lowest level on record in September as high gas prices further soured Americans’ views of the economy. The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index for September dipped to 48.1, notching a 7% decline from August and a nearly 13% drop from a year ago, according to data released Friday. After navigating a once-in-a-century global pandemic, US households have had to contend with higher-than-normal inflation – and the compounding effects of fast-rising prices – for the past five and a half years.
